claims.text: The initial HfZrTiTa0.53 alloy is produced by conventional casting.
As-cast HfZrTiTa0.53 has a fine, homogeneous BCC microstructure.
As-cast HfZrTiTa0.53 has a yield strength of approximately 786 MPa.
As-cast HfZrTiTa0.53 has a compressive strength of approximately 1314 MPa.
As-cast HfZrTiTa0.53 has approximately 13.5% uniform tensile strain.
Annealing HfZrTiTa0.53 at 800–950°C for 10–15 minutes followed by rapid quenching will modify its microstructure.
The annealing treatment will generate uniformly distributed nanoscale precipitates or a bimodal grain structure.
The proposed nanoscale precipitates will be Hf-rich.
The proposed bimodal structure will contain fine matrix regions and locally ductile coarse regions near grain boundaries.
The annealing-induced microstructure will reduce or blunt stress concentrations.
The annealing-induced microstructure will impede premature dislocation localization.
Reduced stress concentration and dislocation localization will delay necking during tensile deformation.
The treatment will not significantly alter the phases responsible for strength and impact-triggered energy release.
Annealing will increase uniform tensile elongation from approximately 13.5% to approximately 20% or more.
After annealing, yield strength will remain within ±10% of the as-cast value.
After annealing, compressive strength will remain within ±10% of the as-cast value.
After annealing, impact-triggered energy release will remain within ±10% of the as-cast value.
The tensile and compression predictions are limited to room temperature and a quasi-static strain rate of approximately 10^-3 s^-1.
The impact-energy prediction is limited to room temperature and a strain rate of approximately 10^3 s^-1.
